title: A Song Is Born: window washers who scat and play boogie
summary: He lists the cast and says Buck and Bubbles played window washers with scat and a boogie, with no singing or dancing.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Continuing on from Atlantic City, the next film in 1947 was "A Song is Born." We'll finish off this tape and continue the description of that film tomorrow, but if you'd like to just sing one of the songs from "A Song is Born" it would be

I can't sing from "A Song is Born," there ain't no song. I just dances only and Buck played the piano. Benny Goodman and all the rest of the musicians played on the instruments, had a jam session with it.
Who else was in that film?
Louis Armstrong, Benny Goodman, [Walter] Sid Catlett Danny Kaye and the Lane Sisters,
Did you dance in that film?

No -- what we did with comedy was talkin' -- what we were talking about was funny concerning the re-baba-rebab-boom, scat, you know, that's all we did is scat, and Buck played the piano, played "Aneetra's (?)Boogie." That's all we did. We were window washers, you know. That was the end of what we did. There ain't no more.

It's a disgrace when you think about it. We had more talent than anybody in the whole picture but didn't get a chance to display it. Buck would play the piano and I'd just do a little shuffle, which was nothin', not even a dance and I didn't get to sing. They smother you, they smother you. I just did a step called "Smother Me," that's what it is, smother me. So what can I do? Can't do nothin'.
